page: Microsoft Azure D8s_v3 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DSv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor operating at 2.3 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes hyper-threading, a 50 MB L3 cache, and support for AVX, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA instruction sets, though it lacks AVX-512 capabilities. The server is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core, and includes 66 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capability. No GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data indicates that the D8s_v3 exhibits modest performance characteristics. Its single-core processing capabilities are positioned in the lower tiers, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1246.28 and a Geekbench single-core score of 848.0, both falling into the bottom 10% to 25% of tested hardware. Multi-core performance is relatively stronger, achieving an average rating in stress-ng multi-core (6563.83) and PassMark CPU physics (859.11), though the overall Geekbench multi-core score of 3121.0 remains in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is constrained, with uncached read and write speeds of 35.34 GB/sec and 21.67 GB/sec respectively. For lightweight workloads, the instance handles small-model LLM inference at average speeds, processing 411.44 tokens/sec for prompts and 157.1 tokens/sec for text generation using a 135M parameter model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D8s_v3 offers a balanced resource density of vCPUs to memory, making it a viable option for legacy general-purpose applications where peak compute performance is not the primary requirement. However, its weak performance in database operations and Redis SET operations suggests it is less suited for high-throughput database hosting. The instance is best utilized for moderate web serving, basic software compilation, lightweight background processing, and development or testing environments that benefit from dedicated vCPUs and Premium Storage compatibility without requiring high-speed memory bandwidth or advanced vector extensions.
